draft.title: The fluid mosaic model
card: The plasma membrane is made of a phospholipid bilayer: two layers of phospholipids. Each phospholipid has a water-loving head and two water-fearing tails.
The heads face the watery fluid inside and outside the cell. The tails face each other in the middle, away from water.
Proteins, cholesterol and carbohydrates are scattered through or on the bilayer. Cholesterol sits between phospholipids. Carbohydrates are attached to the outer surface.
The parts can move sideways within the layer, so the membrane is fluid. The mix of different parts looks like a mosaic, so the model is called fluid mosaic.
draft.remember: The membrane is a flexible bilayer with mixed parts that can move within it.

a.q: In the plasma membrane, why do the phospholipid tails face the middle of the bilayer?
opts: They are water-fearing, so they face away from water
They are water-loving, so they face towards water
They bond to the cholesterol in the centre
They are attached to carbohydrates on the outside
a.why: The tails are water-fearing, so they point inwards, away from the watery fluid on both sides of the membrane. The heads are the water-loving part, and they face the fluid.
a.clue: Think about which part of a phospholipid avoids water.

b.q: A student studies a plasma membrane and sees that its proteins are not fixed in one place but drift sideways. Which part of the fluid mosaic model does this show?
opts: The membrane is fluid because its parts can move
The membrane is a mosaic because it has two layers
The membrane is fluid because it has no proteins
The membrane is a mosaic because its parts are fixed
b.why: Parts that drift sideways within the layer make the membrane fluid. The mosaic describes the mixture of different parts, not the two layers of the bilayer.
b.clue: Fluid describes movement, and mosaic describes the mix of parts.

a.best: They are water-fearing, so they face away from water

b.best: The membrane is fluid because its parts can move
